records.source: תְּפִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥דהַטֵּֽה־יְהוָ֣ה אָזְנְךָ֣ עֲנֵ֑נִי כִּֽי־עָנִ֖י וְאֶבְי֣וֹן אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: A prayer of David. Incline, YHWH, your ear; answer me, for poor and needy [am] I.
pieces: A prayer of David. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear toward me and answer, \q because I am afflicted and in need.

L.1: A prayer of David. \q Incline, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear; answer me, \q for poor and needy [am] I.

R.1: A prayer by David. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please listen to me and answer me. \q I am poor, and I need help.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the one psalm of David in Book Three
decisions.reason: Book Three (Psalms 73-89) is mostly psalms of Asaph and of the sons of Korah; this is its only psalm with David's name. It is a prayer made largely of phrases found in other psalms and in Exodus 34:6 (verse 15).

decisions.choice: incline your ear: bend down and listen
decisions.reason: Asking God to stretch out or bend his ear is asking him to listen closely, as one leans toward someone who speaks softly (17:6; 31:3).

decisions.choice: poor and needy: helpless and dependent on God
decisions.reason: As in 40:18; the pair describes those who have no help but the LORD.

records.heading: Unite my heart to fear your name

records.source: שָֽׁמְרָ֣ה נַפְשִׁי֮ כִּֽי־חָסִ֪יד אָ֥נִי הוֹשַׁ֣ע עַ֭בְדְּךָ אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֑י הַבּוֹטֵ֥חַ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Guard my soul, for faithful [am] I; save your servant, you, my God, the [one] trusting in you.
pieces: Protect my life, for I am loyal to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You are my God; rescue me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, \q for I trust in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.2: Guard my soul, for faithful [am] I; save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] my God, \q the [one] who trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.2: Keep me alive, because I belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and I am loyal. You are my God. Save me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. \q I trust in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: faithful: loyal to God, one of his own
decisions.reason: The word (chasid) comes from chesed, loyal love. It is not a claim to be without fault, but to belong to God and to be loyal to him within the covenant (4:4; 50:5).

decisions.choice: you, my God: a confession inside the request
alternatives: save your servant who trusts in you, you who are my God
decisions.reason: The words "you, my God" stand between "save your servant" and "who trusts in you". They can be read as "you are my God" or as part of the address. Either way the plea rests on the bond between them.

decisions.choice: my life (B); me (R)
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the whole living self; here the danger is to his life (verse 14).

records.source: חָנֵּ֥נִי אֲדֹנָ֑י כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֥יךָ אֶ֝קְרָ֗א כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Show favor to me, my Lord, for to you I call all the day.
pieces: Lord, show me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor; \q I keep calling to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the whole day through.

L.3: Be gracious to me, my Lord, \q for to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I call all the day.

R.3: Lord, be kind to me. \q I call out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all day.

decisions.choice: my Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: The title 'Adonai means "my Lord", master; it is not the divine name. Psalm 86 uses it seven times (verses 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 15). Literal keeps "my Lord"; Balanced and Readable say "Lord".

decisions.choice: be gracious: show undeserved favor
decisions.reason: The verb (chanan) is to show kindness to someone who has no claim on it (4:2).

records.source: שַׂ֭מֵּחַ נֶ֣פֶשׁ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֥יךָ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י נַפְשִׁ֥י אֶשָּֽׂא׃
records.gloss: Gladden [the] soul of your servant, for to you, my Lord, my soul I lift up.
pieces: Make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant glad, \q for my heart reaches out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord.

L.4: Gladden the soul of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, \q for to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my Lord, I lift up my soul.

R.4: Lord, fill me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, with joy. \q I long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and hope in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart.

decisions.choice: lift up my soul: set my longing and hope on you
decisions.reason: As in 25:1 and 143:8: the whole self is turned toward God in desire and trust.

decisions.choice: my Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: my heart reaches out to you (B); I long for you and hope in you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m1); Literal keeps it.

records.source: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אֲ֭דֹנָי ט֣וֹב וְסַלָּ֑ח וְרַב־חֶ֝֗סֶד לְכָל־קֹרְאֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: For you, my Lord, [are] good and forgiving and great of loyal love to all [who] call you.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord, are good and quick to forgive, \q rich in loyal love to everyone who calls to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.5: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my Lord, [are] good and forgiving, \q and great in loyal love to all who call on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.5: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are good, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are ready to forgive. \q Your faithful love is great for all who call out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: forgiving: ready to pardon
decisions.reason: This adjective (sallach) is found only here, from the verb used for God's pardon (salach). It picks up "forgiving iniquity" in Exodus 34:7.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, covenant love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith within a bond, here the LORD's love for his people. Literal and Balanced say "loyal love", Readable "faithful love".

decisions.choice: my Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: הַאֲזִ֣ינָה יְ֭הוָה תְּפִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝הַקְשִׁ֗יבָה בְּק֣וֹל תַּחֲנוּנוֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: Give ear, YHWH, [to] my prayer, and attend to [the] voice of my pleas.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to my prayer; \q pay attention to my voice as I plead for mercy.

L.6: Give ear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to my prayer, \q and attend to the voice of my pleas for mercy.

R.6: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, listen to my prayer. \q Hear me as I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help.

decisions.choice: pleas: requests for grace
decisions.reason: The word (tachanunim) comes from the verb "be gracious" (verse 3): a cry for favor that cannot be earned (28:2).

records.gloss: In [the] day of my distress I call you, for you answer me.
pieces: On my day of trouble I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q sure that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will answer.

L.7: In [the] day of my distress I call [to] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will answer me.

R.7: When I am in trouble, I call out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You will answer me.

decisions.choice: for you will answer me: the ground of his calling
decisions.reason: He calls because he expects an answer; the verse turns the plea of verse 1 ("answer me") into confidence.

decisions.choice: sure that
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "for" expresses here: the confidence behind the call (m1).

records.gloss: There is none like you among the gods, my Lord, and there are none like your works.
pieces: Lord, no god is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and no one has done works like {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}.

L.8: There is none like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the gods, my Lord, \q and [there are] none like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works.

R.8: Lord, there is no god like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q No one else can do the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do.

decisions.choice: none like you among the gods
decisions.reason: The words echo the song at the sea, "Who is like you among the gods, LORD?" (Exodus 15:11). Speaking of the nations' gods is a way of saying that the LORD is beyond them all; verse 10 says that he alone is God.

decisions.choice: my Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: כָּל־גּוֹיִ֤ם׀אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ יָב֤וֹאוּ׀וְיִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֲדֹנָ֑י וִֽיכַבְּד֣וּ לִשְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: All [the] nations that you have made will come and bow down before you, my Lord, and will glorify your name.
pieces: Every nation {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} formed will come and bow low before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord, \q and give glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.9: All [the] nations that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made \q will come and bow down before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my Lord, \q and they will glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.9: Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made all the nations. \q They will all come and bow down to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q They will honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

decisions.choice: all the nations you have made
decisions.reason: Because God made every nation, every nation belongs to him and will come to worship him (22:28; Isaiah 66:23).

decisions.choice: the nations will come and worship
decisions.reason: Revelation 15:4 takes up this hope in the song of those who overcome: all nations will come and worship before God.

decisions.choice: my Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: כִּֽי־גָד֣וֹל אַ֭תָּה וְעֹשֵׂ֣ה נִפְלָא֑וֹת אַתָּ֖ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: For great [are] you and doing wonders; you [are] God by yourself.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are great, a worker of wonders; \q only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God.

L.10: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] great and doing wonders; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone.

R.10: You are great, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do amazing things. \q Only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God.

decisions.choice: wonders: deeds beyond human power
decisions.reason: The word (nifla'ot) is used for the deeds of the exodus and of creation (78:4; Exodus 3:20).

decisions.choice: you alone are God
decisions.reason: The confession of Deuteronomy 4:35 and of Hezekiah's prayer (Isaiah 37:16, 20). It explains verse 8: the "gods" are no match because there is no other God.

records.source: ה֘וֹרֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה׀דַּרְכֶּ֗ךָ אֲהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּאֲמִתֶּ֑ךָ יַחֵ֥ד לְ֝בָבִ֗י לְיִרְאָ֥ה שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Teach me, YHWH, your way; I will walk in your truth; unite my heart to fear your name.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way, \q and I will live by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth; \q give me a heart set on one thing, to revere {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.11: Teach me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way; \q I will walk in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth; \q unite my heart to fear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.11: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, teach me how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want me to live, and I will follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth. \q Make my heart whole, so that I honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all of it.

decisions.choice: unite my heart: make me single-minded
decisions.reason: A divided heart wavers between God and other things (12:3 "a heart and a heart"). He asks for a heart with one aim, as God promises in Jeremiah 32:39 ("one heart").

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: To walk in God's truth is to live by what he has shown to be true and faithful.

decisions.choice: fear your name: revere God himself
decisions.reason: The "name" is God as he has made himself known; to fear it is reverent awe and obedience, not terror (34:12).

decisions.choice: how you want me to live; honor you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "way" and "fear your name" mean (m2, m3).

records.source: אוֹדְךָ֤׀אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱ֭לֹהַי בְּכָל־לְבָבִ֑י וַאֲכַבְּדָ֖ה שִׁמְךָ֣ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: I will thank you, my Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
pieces: Lord my God, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with my whole heart \q and honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name for all time.

L.12: I will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my Lord my God, with all my heart, \q and I will glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever.

R.12: Lord my God, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart. \q I will honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever.

decisions.choice: with all my heart: the undivided heart
decisions.reason: The whole heart of this verse answers the prayer for an undivided heart in verse 11.

decisions.choice: my Lord: the title 'Adonai
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: כִּֽי־חַ֭סְדְּךָ גָּד֣וֹל עָלָ֑י וְהִצַּ֥לְתָּ נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּחְתִּיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: For your loyal love [is] great toward me, and you have delivered my soul from Sheol lowest.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love for me is great; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have pulled me out of deepest Sheol.

L.13: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love [is] great toward me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have delivered my soul from lowest Sheol.

R.13: Your faithful love for me is so great. \q You have rescued me from the deep place of the dead.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, covenant love
decisions.reason: As in verse 5 (chesed).

decisions.choice: lowest Sheol: the very depths of death
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead (6:6). "Lowest" stresses how near death he came (Deuteronomy 32:22).

decisions.choice: you have delivered: a rescue already given or as good as given
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past. It may recall an earlier rescue, or speak of the rescue he prays for as already certain.

records.source: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀זֵ֘דִ֤ים קָֽמוּ־עָלַ֗י וַעֲדַ֣ת עָ֭רִיצִים בִּקְשׁ֣וּ נַפְשִׁ֑י וְלֹ֖א שָׂמ֣וּךָ לְנֶגְדָּֽם׃
records.gloss: God, arrogant [ones] have risen against me, and a band of ruthless [ones] have sought my soul, and not have they set you before them.
pieces: God, the proud have come at me, \q and a pack of brutal people is hunting for my life; \q they do not keep {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in view.

L.14: God, [the] arrogant have risen up against me, \q and a band of ruthless [ones] has sought my soul, \q and they have not set {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before them.

R.14: God, proud people are attacking me. \q A gang of cruel people wants to kill me. \q They do not care about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at all.

decisions.choice: nearly the same as 54:5
decisions.reason: Psalm 54:5 has the same line with "strangers" (zarim) where this verse has "arrogant" (zedim); the two words differ by one similar letter.

decisions.choice: not set you before them: give God no thought
decisions.reason: To set someone before one's eyes is to keep him in mind (16:8). These people live as if God did not see them.

decisions.choice: they do not keep you in view (B); they do not care about you (R)
alternatives: they have not set you before them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m2).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה אֲ֭דֹנָי אֵל־רַח֣וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: But you, my Lord, [are] God compassionate and gracious, long of anger and great of loyal love and faithfulness.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord, are a God full of compassion and grace, \q slow to grow angry, \q overflowing with loyal love and faithfulness.

L.15: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my Lord, [are] a God compassionate and gracious, \q long of anger, \q and great in loyal love and faithfulness.

R.15: But Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a God who cares and is kind. \q You are slow to become angry. \q Your love is great and faithful, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

decisions.choice: the LORD's own description of himself
decisions.reason: These words are what the LORD proclaimed to Moses when he renewed the covenant after the golden calf (Exodus 34:6). Here they are prayed back to God; see also 103:8, 145:8 and Jonah 4:2. Against the arrogant of verse 14 the psalmist sets who God is.

decisions.choice: long of anger: slow to become angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured by the nostrils (the word 'af); a "long" nose is anger that takes a long time to rise.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, covenant love
decisions.reason: As in verse 5 (chesed).

decisions.choice: you keep your word
decisions.reason: The word ('emet) is firmness, reliability; Readable says what it means for God.

records.source: פְּנֵ֥ה אֵלַ֗י וְחָ֫נֵּ֥נִי תְּנָֽה־עֻזְּךָ֥ לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝הוֹשִׁ֗יעָה לְבֶן־אֲמָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your strength to your servant, and save [the] son of your maidservant.
pieces: Turn to me and show me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor; \q lend {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength, \q and rescue the son of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant woman.

L.16: Turn to me and be gracious to me; \q give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, \q and save the son of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} maidservant.

R.16: Turn to me and be kind to me. \q Make me strong, for I serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Save me. My mother served {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} too, so I have belonged to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} since I was born.

decisions.choice: son of your maidservant: one who belongs to you from birth
decisions.reason: A child born to a household servant belonged to the household from birth (Exodus 23:12). The psalmist calls himself God's servant by birth, as in 116:16.

decisions.choice: my mother served you too, so I have belonged to you since I was born
alternatives: save the son of your servant woman
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: עֲשֵֽׂה־עִמִּ֥י א֗וֹת לְט֫וֹבָ֥ה וְיִרְא֣וּ שֹׂנְאַ֣י וְיֵבֹ֑שׁוּ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עֲזַרְתַּ֥נִי וְנִחַמְתָּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Do with me a sign for good, and [they] may see, those hating me, and be ashamed, for you, YHWH, have helped me and comforted me.
pieces: Give me a sign that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mean me good, \q so that those who hate me see it and are left ashamed, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have come to my aid and brought me comfort.

L.17: Work with me a sign for good, \q that those who hate me may see and be ashamed, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have helped me and comforted me.

R.17: Show me a sign that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are good to me. \q Then the people who hate me will see it and be ashamed. \q They will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have helped me and made me feel better.

decisions.choice: a sign for good: a visible token of your favor
decisions.reason: A sign ('ot) is something that can be seen and points beyond itself. He asks for some clear mark of God's goodwill that even his enemies will notice.

decisions.choice: for you have helped me: what the enemies will see
decisions.reason: The last clause says what will put the enemies to shame: that the LORD has taken the psalmist's side. The past tense may also express his confidence.

decisions.choice: they will know that
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link to the enemies' shame explicit (m2).
